subject: maths
question: The marked price of 42 items was equal to the cost price of 70 items. The selling price of 25 items was equal to the marked price of 21 items. Calculate the percentage profit or loss from the sale of each item.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of MP to CP = 70 ÷ 42 = 5/3

Ratio of SP to MP = 21 ÷ 25

Multiply both ratios to find SP/CP: (SP/MP) × (MP/CP) = (21/25) × (5/3) = 7/5

Profit % = [(SP − CP) / CP] × 100 = [(7 − 5) / 5] × 100 = 40%

**∴ The correct answer is 40%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

42 × Marked Price (MP) = 70 × Cost Price (CP)

25 × Selling Price (SP) = 21 × Marked Price (MP)

**Formula Used:**

Profit = SP − CP

Profit % = (Profit / CP) × 100
